unite_adi: UPPER SECONDARY-PREP YEAR-LEVEL: A2 - THEME 2: CLASSROOM LIFE

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students write and design ''my ideal classroom with ideal activities'' project. They will describe ideal roles, relationships, routines, and activities for an ideal class and classroom. They will write scripts for each role. In the class, they will act-out these roles. The assignment will be evaluated by using rubrics. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''classroom life with its components such as classroom rules and instructions; roles, responsibilities and relationships in the classroom; daily and study routines and learning activities in the classroom'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school may know classroom rules and instructions; roles, responsibilities and relationships in the classroom; daily and study routines and learning activities in the classroom mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''classroom life'' in English from previous themes and/or years such as ''an essay, a lecture, a task, and so on'' and also some structures such as ''Students present their essays. We can work together in this activity.'' in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''classroom rules and instructions; roles, responsibilities and relationships in the classroom; daily and study routines and learning activities in the classroom'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To help students improve their writing skills in English by editing/correcting a poorly written classroom instructions guidebook by using the target vocabulary and functions accurately. Objective: To write and correct classroom rules and instructions in English by using the target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: Fix the ''Classroom Instructions Guidebook'' Students work in groups to correct/edit and improve a poorly written ''Classroom Instructions Guidebook'', including unclear rules or incorrect grammar (e.g., ''No speak when teacher teaching'', ''Do your homework always!''). Without a word bank, students use their knowledge and creativity to rewrite the guidebook with accurate vocabulary and grammar including imperatives, modals (can, shall), and adverbs of frequency. Groups aim to produce clear and well-structured rules such as ''Don’t talk while your teacher is talking'', or ''Always complete your homework on time''. The group that correctly and quickly completes the task wins. Finally, each group presents their revised Guidebook to the class, explaining their changes, and the teacher provides constructive and encouraging feedback. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Objective: To improve students’ writing and communication skills in English by creating and performing a short drama about classroom life, using target vocabulary for rules, roles, routines, and target grammar. Objective: To create and perform a short drama about classroom rules, roles, routines in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 2: Create a Classroom Drama Script Students work in small groups to create a short drama script based on a classroom scenario, such as ''A new student joins the class and learns the rules'', or ''Students work together to complete a group project''. The script must include imperatives (e.g., ''Follow the teacher’s instructions!''), social language expressions (e.g., ''Thank you for your help!''), and modals (e.g., ''Can we work together on this project?'', ''Shall we ask the teacher for help?''). After writing, groups perform their drama, paying special attention to accurate language use and pronunciation. In the end, the teacher and classmates provide constructive feedback on language use, creativity, and performance. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To improve students’ communication skills in English on ''classroom rules and instructions'', by using the target vocabulary through group collaboration and friendly competition. Objective: To describe classroom rules and instructions in English by using the target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: Classroom Rules Miming The teacher prepares cards with visuals representing classroom rules (e.g., a picture of a raised hand for ''Raise your hand to speak!''). Students work in groups. In groups, one student selects a card, keeps it hidden, and acts out the rule shown on the visual without speaking. The group has a set time limit (e.g., 1 minute) to guess the rule and form a correct sentence about it (e.g., ''We must raise our hands to speak in class''). Correct guesses and accurate sentences earn points for the group. The activity continues in turns, and the group with the highest points in the end becomes the winner, promoting active engagement and teamwork. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Objective: To improve students’ communication skills in English on ''classroom rules and instructions'', through interactive and collaborative activities. Objective: To describe and talk about classroom rules and instructions in English by using the target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 2: Visual Rules and Roles Matching The teacher creates cards that visually represent classroom rules and roles, such as raising a hand to speak or pointing to the board to explain a lesson. The teacher also creates text cards with simple English descriptions of the rules and roles. Students work in pairs or small groups to match the visual cards with their corresponding text cards. For a digital option, the teacher can use a web 2.0 tool, where students drag and drop virtual visuals to their matching text descriptions. Once matched, each group reads the rule or role aloud and explains it in a full sentence, such as ''This rule means we must raise our hands before speaking'', or ''The teacher explains the lesson clearly to the students''. At the end of the activity, both the teacher and classmates provide constructive feedback on the accuracy and clarity of the group’s explanations. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
